card.text: Explore Borrelly's MICAS photograph and independent USGS and DLR terrain reconstructions.

introduction.text: Deep Space 1 flew past Borrelly in September 2001. Its images revealed an elongated nucleus with smooth terrain, rough slopes and a narrow waist. The grid marks an estimated shape where terrain was not measured.

micas.title: Encounter photograph
micas.summary: The mission team’s orthophoto laid onto USGS terrain, keeping the lighting seen by Deep Space 1. The grid covers missing imagery and the estimated far side.

usgs.title: USGS stereo terrain
usgs.summary: Terrain reconstructed from overlapping MICAS images, with manual stereo checks. Gray shows measured terrain; the grid fills the far side with an estimated shape.

dlr.title: DLR stereo terrain
dlr.summary: An independent reconstruction of the encounter images, aligned with USGS at the same scale. The grid marks gaps and the estimated far side.

height.title: Above the image plane
height.summary: Height toward the spacecraft from the source’s reference plane. This is not distance from the comet’s centre. Turn Shadows off to read the scale.

difference.title: USGS minus DLR
difference.summary: USGS height minus DLR height after alignment. Colors show model disagreement, not change over time; gray marks missing overlap. Turn Shadows off to read the scale.
